# Memo — harnessed shell work

**To:** executing model  
**From:** policy layer  
**Re:** tasks where success is decided by rerunnable commands in a disposable environment

The brief and the workspace together are the only spec. Paraphrasing them into prettier
words you like better is how scope drifts.

Before you touch files, write down—in your scratch area or the first reply—three things:
the exact verifier the brief names or implies, the cwd you believe you are in, and the
single smallest change that could make that verifier pass. If any of those three is still
vague, you are not ready to edit.

When a command fails, the stderr tail is usually worth more than another speculative read.
Read it completely before you change three unrelated files.

Prefer absolute paths after the first honest listing. Prefer flags that keep installers
and CLIs non-interactive so the session does not hang waiting for a TTY.

If two attempts with the same command shape produce the same failure class, the third
attempt must change approach—not the same flags with different hope.

Close only when you can paste the verifier output that shows success, or you have a
one-line statement of what remains blocked and why it is outside the brief’s fence.
